couplets.gloss: Foolishness means letting go of what does you good and hanging on to what does you harm.

edges.reason: Answers its own question: folly is dropping what profits and gripping what harms.
edges.quote: taking hold of what harms you and letting go of what profits you

couplets.gloss: The very worst foolishness is wanting to do things that are beneath you.
keywords: doing what you know is wrong

edges.reason: Ranks setting your heart on conduct that isn’t for you as the worst folly there is.
edges.quote: The worst folly of all

couplets.gloss: A fool feels no shame, shirks what needs doing, has no warmth for anyone and looks after nothing worth keeping.

edges.reason: Lists the fool’s habits: no shame, no inquiry, no warmth, no care for anything.
edges.quote: these are a fool’s habits

couplets.gloss: Nobody is a bigger fool than an educated person who teaches others how to behave but can't govern himself.

edges.reason: Study and teaching don’t save someone without self-control from being the worst fool of all.
edges.quote: No one is a greater fool

edges.reason: Self-control is the one thing all that learning lacks, and the lack makes a fool.
edges.quote: still has no self-control

couplets.gloss: In one lifetime a fool can do enough harm to bring suffering on himself through every life to come.

edges.reason: One birth of foolishness is enough to spoil all the births after it.
edges.quote: the mire of hell for all seven births

edges.reason: Misery is a crop the fool plants now and reaps across lifetimes.
edges.quote: sowing in one birth the seeds of misery

couplets.gloss: Put a fool in charge of serious work and he not only wrecks it but may end up in chains for it.

edges.reason: A fool who takes on a task without knowing how wrecks it and lands in fetters.
edges.quote: the fool ends up in fetters

couplets.gloss: If a fool comes into big money, outsiders live well off it while his own family goes hungry.

edges.reason: A fool’s wealth feeds outsiders and leaves his own people hungry.
edges.quote: strangers eat their fill and the fool’s own people go hungry

couplets.gloss: Give a fool something valuable and he acts like someone unhinged who has also been drinking.

edges.reason: Anything of value sends a fool as wild as a drunken lunatic.
edges.quote: like a madman getting drunk

couplets.gloss: Being friends with fools has one great charm: you feel no sorrow at all when it ends.

edges.reason: Mock praise: the one pleasure of befriending fools is that parting does not hurt.
edges.quote: When it ends, it brings no pain at all

couplets.gloss: A fool walking in among good people is like someone putting a dirty foot on a clean bed.

edges.reason: A fool among the worthy soils the gathering as an unwashed foot soils a bed.
edges.quote: an unwashed foot on a bed

couplets.gloss: Lack of sense is the real poverty: people hardly count any other kind of want as being poor.

edges.reason: Counts a lack of understanding as the one true poverty.
edges.quote: The worst poverty is a lack of understanding

edges.reason: Moves the word poverty onto understanding, and says no other lack deserves it.
edges.quote: does not count any other lack as poverty

couplets.gloss: When a fool gives something willingly, the credit belongs to the receiver's good luck and nothing else.

edges.reason: A gift from someone without understanding earns the giver no credit: the receiver’s penance brought it about.
edges.quote: nothing but the penance of the one who receives

couplets.gloss: A senseless person does himself more damage than his worst enemies could ever manage.

edges.reason: People without understanding cause themselves more pain than their enemies could.
edges.quote: hard even for their enemies to cause

couplets.gloss: Real shallowness is telling yourself how clever you are.

edges.reason: Pins it to one inner voice, the conceit that tells itself it is wise.
edges.quote: the conceit that says, “I am wise.”

couplets.gloss: Claim to know what you don't, and people start doubting even what you really do know.

edges.reason: Pretending to learning casts doubt even on what you have truly mastered.
edges.quote: makes people doubt even what you have truly mastered

couplets.gloss: What's the point of a fool covering his body while the flaws in his character stay on open show?

edges.reason: Mocks a modesty that clothes the body and leaves your own faults bare.
edges.quote: leave your own faults uncovered

couplets.gloss: A shallow person who can't keep confidential things to himself does himself terrible harm.

edges.reason: Letting a secret slip is how someone without understanding brings great harm on himself.
edges.quote: lets a precious secret slip

couplets.gloss: Someone who won't take direction and can't work out what's right alone is a burden on others all his life.

edges.reason: He won’t do as he is told and can’t see for himself, and all his life he is a disease.
edges.quote: He won’t act when told and can’t work it out himself

couplets.gloss: Trying to enlighten a fool makes you a fool too: he knows only his own way and can't imagine it's wrong.

edges.reason: The man who can’t see holds to what he saw and can’t be shown anything else.
edges.quote: goes on seeing it the way he saw it

edges.reason: Turns the whole problem into sight: a man who can’t see, and a teacher who ends up seeing nothing.
edges.quote: a man who can’t see

edges.reason: Tells anyone still arguing that whoever tries to show such a man ends up seeing nothing himself.
edges.quote: ends up seeing nothing himself

couplets.gloss: Anyone who flatly denies what everyone else knows to be so gets treated as something less than human.

edges.reason: Denying what the world affirms earns the name of a demon.
edges.quote: will be counted a demon on this earth

couplets.gloss: Hostility is a sickness in every living being, and it spreads the disease of hatred and division.

edges.reason: Calls strife the disease that feeds division in every living being.
edges.quote: They call strife the disease

edges.reason: Frames strife as a disease that spreads division through all that lives.
edges.quote: the disease that feeds, in every living being, the fault of drawing apart

couplets.gloss: Even if a neighbour sets out to hurt you and start a quarrel, the best course is not to hit back.
couplets.sensitive: Counsels not answering deliberate injury

edges.reason: Rules out answering with harm, even against someone who injures you on purpose.
edges.quote: it is best not to answer with harm

edges.reason: Asks that harm not be returned, even when the other began it.
edges.quote: not to answer with harm

edges.reason: Speaks to someone set on a break with you, and says not to answer with harm.
edges.quote: means to break with you

couplets.gloss: The urge to oppose everyone is a painful sickness, and anyone who gets rid of it wins a name that lasts.

edges.reason: Promises undying brightness to whoever gets rid of strife.
edges.quote: the painful disease called strife

edges.reason: Treats strife as a sickness you can be rid of.
edges.quote: Get rid of the painful disease

couplets.gloss: Get rid of hostility, the worst of all miseries, and the greatest happiness comes within your reach.

edges.reason: Ranks strife the worst of all pains, and its end the greatest joy.
edges.quote: strife, the worst pain of all pains

couplets.gloss: No one wants to bring down a person who is skilled at stepping back from conflict.

edges.reason: Shows the safety of the opposite: nobody tries to beat those who turn aside from strife.
edges.quote: those who can turn aside from strife

couplets.gloss: Whoever enjoys getting the better of others in a fight is close to his own collapse.

edges.reason: Relish for strife means the ruin of your own life is close.
edges.quote: calls it sweet to press on in strife

couplets.gloss: People with a spiteful mind who love strife can't see the real way to get ahead.

edges.reason: A taste for strife blinds people of bitter understanding to the truth that brings victory.
edges.quote: can’t see the truth that brings victory

couplets.gloss: Backing away from a fight brings you prosperity, but let it escalate and ruin follows close behind.

edges.reason: Press on in strife, and ruin presses on to meet you.
edges.quote: ruin presses on towards you

edges.reason: Gives the choice plainly: step back and prosper, or let the quarrel grow and be ruined.
edges.quote: Turning aside from strife brings gain

couplets.gloss: A person on the way up shrugs off provocation, while one heading for ruin lets his hostility run without limit.

edges.reason: Reads a wish to increase strife as the sign that a man is already headed for ruin.
edges.quote: To bring about his own ruin, he looks to increase it

couplets.gloss: Hostility is the source of everything unpleasant, while friendliness brings the pride of living in peace with others.

edges.reason: Traces everything bitter in life back to this one source.
edges.quote: Strife brings all that is bitter

couplets.gloss: Don't take on anyone stronger than you, but keep up unrelenting pressure on those who are weaker.
couplets.sensitive: Urges relentless war on the weak

edges.reason: Sorts foes by strength: leave the powerful alone and press the weak without pause.
edges.quote: seek enmity with the weak

edges.reason: Whom to fight is settled by weighing one's force against theirs.
edges.quote: opposing the strong

edges.reason: Its first clause is direct advice to one facing a stronger opponent: don’t stand against them.
edges.quote: Keep from opposing the strong

couplets.gloss: Someone with no love for others, no strong allies and no strength of his own cannot hold out against an enemy.
Someone who is fearful, ignorant, ungenerous and unable to get along with others is easy prey for any enemy.

edges.reason: Fear comes first among the lacks that make him easy for his enemies.
edges.quote: He fears

edges.reason: No understanding is the second gap his foes can use.
edges.quote: he doesn’t understand

edges.reason: Refusing to give completes the list of what he is without.
edges.quote: he won’t give

couplets.gloss: Someone who never lets go of anger and has no self-restraint is easy for anybody to beat, anywhere, at any time.

edges.reason: A temper that never cools hands victory to anyone, at any time or place.
edges.quote: doesn’t give up anger

couplets.gloss: Someone who ignores sound method, does nothing fitting, shrugs off disgrace and lacks character is a gift to his enemies.

edges.reason: Not minding blame is among the faults that make him sweet to his enemies.
edges.quote: doesn’t mind blame

couplets.gloss: A person ruled by blind rage and excessive lust is the kind of enemy others are glad to have.

edges.reason: Boundless desire makes a man’s enmity something his foes welcome.
edges.quote: overflowing desire

edges.reason: Anger that blinds a man leaves an opponent whose enmity is worth wanting.
edges.quote: blinding anger

couplets.gloss: It is worth paying to have as your enemy someone who takes a project on and then does everything that sabotages it.

edges.reason: Names the one opponent worth paying for: the man who undermines his own undertaking.
edges.quote: Even if you must pay for it, be sure to get the enmity

couplets.gloss: Someone with no good qualities and many faults ends up without allies, which suits his enemies perfectly.
Nothing delights an enemy more than facing someone both foolish and frightened.

edges.reason: A frightened opponent is what foes most hope to meet.
edges.quote: is full of fear

edges.reason: Having no understanding gives a man’s enemies joy that is never far away.
edges.quote: has no understanding

edges.reason: Takes the enemy's side of the matter: what he most delights to find in an opponent.
edges.quote: joy is never far away

couplets.gloss: Whoever won't even take on a foolish neighbour for an easy win will never know glory.
couplets.sensitive: Ties glory to attacking a weak neighbour

edges.reason: Refusing even the small prize of fighting an unlearned man shuts you out of glory for good.
edges.quote: glory will never come to you

couplets.gloss: Hostility is a wretched thing and should never be invited, not even as a joke.

edges.reason: So graceless a thing that no one should want it, even in jest.
edges.quote: No one should want it, even in jest

couplets.gloss: Make enemies of soldiers if you must, but never make an enemy of those who fight with words.

edges.reason: Rates the ploughmen of the word as more dangerous to cross than those of the bow.
edges.quote: ploughmen whose plough is the word

edges.reason: The archer is the lesser danger against which the speaker is measured.
edges.quote: ploughmen whose plough is the bow

edges.reason: Both are ploughmen here, one with the bow for a plough and one with the word.
edges.quote: whose plough is the word

couplets.gloss: Anyone who takes on many enemies alone and without allies is more foolish than someone who has lost his mind.

edges.reason: Calling many foes down on oneself with no ally is worse than madness.
edges.quote: more foolish than the mad

edges.reason: One man against a multitude has plainly not weighed his force against theirs.
edges.quote: stands alone and makes enemies of many

couplets.gloss: Someone with the grace to turn enemies into friends has the whole world resting on his greatness.

edges.reason: Praises making friends of enemies as the way to hold the world.
edges.quote: make friends of enemies

couplets.gloss: If you are alone against two enemies, make one of them your ally.

edges.reason: Outnumbered and alone, one should split the pair by winning one of them over.
edges.quote: Make one of the two your good ally

couplets.gloss: While you are in trouble, don't commit to anyone as friend or foe: leave him alone until it passes.

edges.reason: A time of ruin is the wrong time to fix anyone as friend or foe.
edges.quote: in a time of ruin

couplets.gloss: Don't pour out your troubles to people who can't grasp them, and don't let enemies see where you are weak.
couplets.sensitive: Could deter someone in distress from confiding

edges.reason: Hides what could be used against one: troubles from the unknowing, weak spots from foes.
edges.quote: Don’t show weakness to your enemies

couplets.gloss: Work out your plan, build up your strength and secure your defences, and your enemies' pride will soon fall.

edges.reason: Knowing the way, building yourself up and guarding yourself are what bring a proud enemy down.
edges.quote: Know the way, build yourself up and guard yourself

edges.reason: Names the enemy's pride as the thing such readiness will bring low.
edges.quote: your enemies’ pride will die

couplets.gloss: Cut down a thorn bush while it is young: once it hardens it will wound whoever tries to remove it.

edges.reason: Deal with a foe early, before he grows strong enough to wound the hand.
edges.quote: while it is young

edges.reason: The young thorn-tree stands for an enemy still small enough to fell.
edges.quote: Kill a thorn tree while it is young

couplets.gloss: Those who can't break the pride of people who oppose them won't survive for long.

edges.reason: Gives short life to those who leave the pride of their foes unbroken.
edges.quote: fail to crush the pride of their foes

couplets.gloss: Even shade and water are unwelcome if they make you ill, and so are relatives who are out to harm you.

edges.reason: Your own people turn as bad as sickening shade and water when they do you harm.
edges.quote: Your own people’s ways are bad too, if they do you harm

edges.reason: Being your own earns no exemption: relations are judged by what they do to you.
edges.quote: Your own people’s ways

couplets.gloss: Don't be afraid of enemies who come at you openly like a drawn sword: fear the ones who act like friends.

edges.reason: Fears the foe who looks like kin more than any open attacker.
edges.quote: enemies who are like kin

edges.reason: The open enemy is a bare blade, which at least can be seen coming.
edges.quote: enemies who are like swords

edges.reason: Tells someone unsure whom to fear to save that fear for the friendly face, not the open foe.
edges.quote: Fear the company of enemies who are like kin

couplets.gloss: Be on guard against the enemy within: at your weakest moment he will cut you more cleanly than a potter's blade.

edges.reason: The hidden foe waits for one's moment of difficulty, then cuts clean through.
edges.quote: In your moment of weakness

couplets.gloss: An enemy hidden in your circle soon turns your own people against you and brings trouble after trouble.

edges.reason: A hidden foe's first work is to spoil one's own people, and many evils follow.
edges.quote: turn your own people bad

couplets.gloss: When a relative turns against you, the harm is many-sided and can even put your life in danger.

edges.reason: Betrayal from within the family puts life itself at risk.
edges.quote: harms that lead towards death

edges.reason: Takes up the particular case of the relation who turns traitor.
edges.quote: an enemy within appears who is close by kinship

couplets.gloss: Once division breaks out among your closest people, it's nearly impossible to escape being destroyed by it.

edges.reason: Discord among those closest makes death hard to escape, at any time.
edges.quote: it is always hard to escape death

couplets.gloss: A household at odds with itself is like a pot and its lid: it looks like one thing but never truly joins.

edges.reason: A split family keeps the look of one piece, like a casket and its lid, but is never whole.
edges.quote: may seem to fit together, but it never joins

couplets.gloss: A family torn by inner conflict wears away bit by bit, like iron being filed down.

edges.reason: An enemy inside a family wears its strength away.
edges.quote: wears away its strength

edges.reason: Gold under the file pictures a family worn away stroke by stroke.
edges.quote: Like gold rubbed by a file

couplets.gloss: However small the rift, even as tiny as a crack in a sesame seed, inner division means ruin is coming.

edges.reason: No enemy within is too small: one the size of a split sesame seed still holds ruin.
edges.quote: as small as a split sesame seed

couplets.gloss: Living closely with someone who is not truly with you is like sharing a small hut with a snake.

edges.reason: Close daily life with those not of one mind with you is a standing danger.
edges.quote: those who are not of one mind with you

edges.reason: The snake in the hut is a danger too near to step away from.
edges.quote: sharing a hut with a snake

edges.reason: Names the risk of staying intimate with someone whose heart is against you.
edges.quote: Living with those who are not of one mind with you

couplets.gloss: If you care about staying safe, the first thing to watch is never to offend those with real power.

edges.reason: Puts not offending the great at the very top of all self-protection.
edges.quote: not to scorn the power of those who can get things done

edges.reason: Sets those who can get things done apart as the ones above all not to scorn.
edges.quote: those who can get things done

couplets.gloss: Disrespect those with great power and they can make your life a misery for good.

edges.reason: A slight to the great comes back as misery with no end.
edges.quote: lasting pain through the great

edges.reason: The great themselves are the means by which the pain comes.
edges.quote: through the great

couplets.gloss: Ignoring good advice and insulting people who can crush you is a sure way to bring about your own downfall.
couplets.sensitive: Mock recipe for one's own destruction; risky read literally

edges.reason: Sarcasm: provoking those who can destroy you is offered as the quick road to disaster.
edges.quote: offend those who can kill the moment they wish

edges.reason: Refusing to listen is the first step in its mocking recipe for ruin.
edges.quote: don’t listen

couplets.gloss: A weak person who insults the powerful is as good as waving death over to come and get him.

edges.reason: For the weak to harm the mighty is to invite their own end.
edges.quote: For the powerless to harm the powerful

edges.reason: Pictures the offender calling Death over to him with a wave.
edges.quote: beckoning Death with your hand

couplets.sensitive: Warns the weak against standing up to the powerful.

couplets.gloss: Anger a mighty ruler and there's nowhere you can go where you will thrive.

edges.reason: Whoever draws a strong ruler’s anger finds no refuge anywhere.
edges.quote: will live nowhere

couplets.gloss: You might survive being caught in a fire, but there is no surviving the wrong you do to the great.

edges.reason: Rates a wrong done to the mighty as harder to survive than a blaze.
edges.quote: Those who offend the great will not survive

edges.reason: Sets a fire one might live through against an offence one will not.
edges.quote: survive being burned by fire

couplets.gloss: A rich life and great wealth mean nothing once truly great people of spiritual power are angry with you.

edges.reason: A splendid life and vast wealth count for nothing once the worthy turn in anger.
edges.quote: if the truly worthy turn in anger on you

couplets.gloss: Even rulers who seem secure for ever will vanish with all their family if those as great as mountains turn against them.

edges.reason: People who seem fixed on the earth vanish, with their families, at the mere will of the great.
edges.quote: vanish, with their families

edges.reason: Measures the stature of the great by the mountain.
edges.quote: those who are like mountains

couplets.gloss: An angry glance from people bound by sacred vows could topple Indra himself from his throne.

edges.reason: The anger of those with lofty vows is enough to unseat a ruler.
edges.quote: even a ruler breaks midway and loses his rule

edges.reason: Places those of lofty vows above even a ruler.
edges.quote: those of lofty vows

couplets.gloss: No backing, however strong, can rescue you once spiritually mighty people turn against you.

edges.reason: The greatest support gives no protection from the anger of those of surpassing worth.
edges.quote: Even those with the greatest of supports won’t survive

couplets.gloss: A man wrapped up in doting on his wife won't achieve much; those set on big things keep clear of that.
couplets.sensitive: Treats devotion to a wife as a lure away from greatness

edges.reason: Sets doting on a wife against any hope of the finest reward.
edges.quote: Men who dote on their wives

edges.reason: Speaks to men as husbands, and says those set on action want no part of this.
edges.quote: Men who are set on action

couplets.gloss: A man obsessed with his wife and careless of all else is an embarrassment however well he is doing.
couplets.sensitive: Holds a man's love for his wife up to public shame

edges.reason: Even his gains become a great disgrace once he craves a woman, careless of all else.
edges.quote: become a great disgrace

couplets.gloss: A husband who abases himself to his spouse can never face decent people without embarrassment.
couplets.sensitive: Treats deferring to a wife as shameful weakness

edges.reason: Bowing to his wife brings a man shame among good people.
edges.quote: always bring you shame among good people

edges.reason: Singles out the husband by what he does before his wife.
edges.quote: bowing to your wife

couplets.gloss: However capable a man is, his abilities earn no regard if he is frightened of his wife.
couplets.sensitive: Scorns a man who fears his wife; could reach an abused husband

edges.reason: Fear of his wife strips a man's abilities of any standing.
edges.quote: A man who fears his wife

couplets.gloss: A husband scared of his spouse won't dare do a good turn, even for people who deserve it.
couplets.sensitive: Blames a frightened husband; could reach someone abused at home

edges.reason: Fear of his wife reaches outward and stops him doing good even to good people.
edges.quote: afraid to do good to good people

couplets.gloss: Men in awe of their wives' embrace get no respect, however grandly they live.
couplets.sensitive: Shames men for being in awe of their wives

edges.reason: Living like the gods earns nothing for men who fear their wives’ shoulders.
edges.quote: men who fear their wives’ bamboo shoulders have no standing

couplets.gloss: A modest young woman has more dignity than a man who spends his life doing a woman's bidding.
couplets.sensitive: Treats a woman's lead as beneath a man's dignity

edges.reason: Ranks such a man’s manhood below the greatness of a woman with modesty.
edges.quote: A woman with modesty has more greatness

couplets.gloss: Men who do whatever their wives want won't come through for friends or do any good.
couplets.sensitive: Blames a wife's influence for a man's failures

edges.reason: Being governed at home is said to cost a man his duty to friends and all good works.
edges.quote: won’t meet their friends’ needs and won’t do good

couplets.gloss: Men who take orders from their wives will miss out on goodness, wealth and the rest of life's aims.
couplets.sensitive: Says a wife's direction empties a man's life of all good

edges.reason: Holds that nothing worth having survives in a man who does a woman’s bidding.
edges.quote: those who do a woman’s bidding

edges.reason: Counts what such a man loses: righteous acts, wealth and other deeds, the aims of life.
edges.quote: Righteous acts, great wealth and other deeds

couplets.gloss: People with thoughtful minds and firm character never fall into the foolishness of doting on a woman.
couplets.sensitive: Calls a man's devotion to his wife folly

edges.reason: Claims those with a broad, thinking heart never give way to this, and calls it folly.
edges.quote: the folly that comes of clinging to a woman

couplets.gloss: Women who want a man for his money, not out of love, have sweet talk that ends only in his ruin.
couplets.sensitive: Portrays sex workers as mercenary deceivers

edges.reason: Describes them by what they want: wealth and not love.
edges.quote: who want wealth and not love

edges.reason: Warns the man drawn to her that the sweet talk ends only in misery.
edges.quote: their cajoleries will lead only to misery

couplets.gloss: Women whose sweet words are aimed only at what they can get should be weighed up and kept at arm's length.
couplets.sensitive: Portrays paid women as scheming; advises shunning them

edges.reason: Takes talk of virtue with an eye to gain as their mark, and says to keep away.
edges.quote: Weigh their ways and keep away

couplets.gloss: The embrace of a woman paid for it is false, as empty as holding a stranger's corpse in the dark.
couplets.sensitive: Likens a sex worker's embrace to a corpse

edges.reason: Names the paid embrace as false, like holding a stranger’s corpse in the dark.
edges.quote: The false embrace

couplets.gloss: People whose minds are on goodness don't sink to the cheap pleasures sold by women who want only money.
couplets.sensitive: Calls sex workers defiling

edges.reason: Those who look to compassion are known by keeping clear of a bought embrace.
edges.quote: won’t touch the cheap charms

couplets.gloss: People of sharp judgment and deep learning don't go near the cheap pleasures that are open to anyone for a price.
couplets.sensitive: Treats women open to all as defiling

edges.reason: A good mind joined to understanding is what holds people back here.
edges.quote: won’t touch the cheap charms of women who are common to all

couplets.gloss: Those who want to protect their own good name stay away from women who parade their charms for sale.
couplets.sensitive: Uses contemptuous language for sex workers

edges.reason: Those who spread their own goodness are said to stay out of paid embraces.
edges.quote: Those who spread their own goodness

edges.reason: Pictures the woman as spreading her cheap charms about.
edges.quote: spread their cheap charms about

couplets.gloss: Only weak-minded men go looking for women whose bodies are present while their thoughts are elsewhere.
couplets.sensitive: Demeans sex workers as bodies without feeling

edges.reason: Going after an embrace with no heart in it marks an unsteady mind.
edges.quote: Those without a steady heart

couplets.gloss: For men who can't judge well, the embrace of deceptive women is like falling under a demon's spell.
couplets.sensitive: Casts women as wily spirits who ensnare men

edges.reason: Those without sharp understanding are struck by such embraces as by a deadly spirit.
edges.quote: a deadly spirit’s touch

couplets.gloss: A dressed-up woman for hire and her gentle embrace are the pit of filth that worthless men sink into.
couplets.sensitive: Compares a sex worker to a filthy ditch

edges.reason: Makes those shoulders the mire of hell where only worthless low men sink.
edges.quote: the mire of hell where worthless low men sink

edges.reason: Begins with their jewels and soft shoulders, and turns them into the danger.
edges.quote: soft shoulders of finely jewelled women

couplets.gloss: Two-timing women, drink and dice are the company kept by men whose luck has left them.
couplets.sensitive: Ranks women of divided heart among the signs of a ruined man

edges.reason: Women of two hearts come first among the friends of those prosperity has left.
edges.quote: Women of two hearts

edges.reason: Drink stands second in this list of what ruined men turn to.
edges.quote: liquor

edges.reason: The dice close the list of friends left to those prosperity has abandoned.
edges.quote: dice

couplets.gloss: Heavy drinkers lose the respect their enemies had for them, and they lose their good name as well.

edges.reason: The drinker stops being feared and loses his glory as well.
edges.quote: are never feared

couplets.gloss: Nobody should drink, unless they are people who don't care what good people think of them.

edges.reason: Forbids drink outright, then grants it only to those who have given up on being respected.
edges.quote: Don’t drink liquor

couplets.gloss: Even the woman who gave birth to him can't bear to see a drunk, so imagine how he looks to decent people.
couplets.sensitive: Shames a person with a drinking problem through his mother's disgust

edges.reason: Even a mother recoils at the sight, and the worthy still more.
edges.quote: hateful even in your mother’s sight

couplets.gloss: Shame, that fine lady, turns her back on anyone given to the disgraceful fault of drinking.

edges.reason: Drink is the low vice that drives away even the sense of shame.
edges.quote: the great, despised fault called liquor

couplets.gloss: It is the height of stupidity to pay good money just to make yourself numb.

edges.reason: Drink goes unnamed, but the trade is plain: wealth paid out for mere senselessness.
edges.quote: Paying out your wealth to buy senselessness

edges.reason: Puts the bargain to the drinker in plain terms: wealth out, senselessness back.
edges.quote: shows you don’t know what to do

couplets.gloss: People who drink toxic liquor every day are no better than the sleeping, and the sleeping no better than the dead.

edges.reason: Calls liquor what it is, a dose of poison.
edges.quote: always drinking poison

edges.reason: Drinkers are set beside sleepers and the dead.
edges.quote: no different from the dead

couplets.gloss: Secret drinkers who spend their days in a stupor get found out by those nearby and laughed at.

edges.reason: Drinking in hiding ends in the laughter of the townsfolk anyway.
edges.quote: laughed at by their townsfolk

edges.reason: Tells the secret drinker that concealment will not hold for long.
edges.quote: who see right through them

couplets.gloss: A drinker should stop claiming he's never been drunk: that only adds a lie to the habit.

edges.reason: Denying the drinking only stacks a lie on top of the vice.
edges.quote: Give up saying, “I have never been drunk.”

edges.reason: Takes away the drinker's plea that he has never been drunk.
edges.quote: “I have never been drunk.”

couplets.gloss: Reasoning with a drunk is like hunting with a torch for someone who has gone under water.

edges.reason: A man in drink is beyond reproof, as far out of reach as one under water.
edges.quote: Reasoning with a drunk

edges.reason: A flame carried down to find a man under water shows how useless reproof is here.
edges.quote: searcheth torch in hand

couplets.gloss: When a sober person looks at someone drunk, can't he imagine how he himself looks after a drink?

edges.reason: Holds up another man's drunken state as a picture of the drinker's own.
edges.quote: sees a drunk man

edges.reason: Asks him to apply to himself what he sees so clearly in another.
edges.quote: doesn’t he think of how he slips when he has drunk?

edges.reason: Gives a sober moment a use: watch someone drunk and see yourself.
edges.quote: sober for the moment

couplets.gloss: Don't gamble even when you are winning: a win is only the hook swallowed by the fish.

edges.reason: Even a win is a trap, the bait on a hook the fish swallows.
edges.quote: Your winnings are a hook swallowed by a fish

edges.reason: Speaks to someone kept at the table by wins: those wins are the hook.
edges.quote: Don’t want gambling, even if you win

couplets.gloss: Gamblers lose a hundred for every one they gain, so how can they ever expect to do well in life?

edges.reason: Does the sum: a hundred lost for each one gained leaves no road to thriving.
edges.quote: gain one and lose a hundred

couplets.gloss: Keep betting on the roll of the dice and everything you own ends up in other people's pockets.

edges.reason: Constant betting moves your wealth and income into other hands.
edges.quote: your wealth and income will leave and go to others

couplets.gloss: Nothing makes you poor as surely as gambling, which destroys your reputation and drags you into shabby acts.

edges.reason: Ranks it the surest road to poverty, shrinking you and ruining your good name.
edges.quote: Nothing brings poverty like gambling

couplets.gloss: Plenty of people have boasted of their luck at dice and been obsessed with the gaming house, and every one of them ended up with nothing.

edges.reason: Allows no exception: those who cling in pride to dice have come to nothing.
edges.quote: have come to nothing

couplets.gloss: People taken over by gambling, as if by the goddess of bad luck, go hungry and suffer every kind of hardship.

edges.reason: The passion leaves its victims starving and in every misery.
edges.quote: won’t fill their bellies, and will suffer

edges.reason: Makes gambling a disguise of Fortune’s dark sister, who covers over those she takes.
edges.quote: the goddess of misfortune called gambling

couplets.gloss: Spend your time in the gambling den and you will lose your family money and your good character.

edges.reason: Time in the gaming hall eats up long-held wealth and good nature.
edges.quote: destroys the wealth and good nature you have long had

couplets.gloss: Gambling eats your money, pushes you into lying, kills your compassion and leaves you miserable.

edges.reason: Follows the damage in order: wealth, then truth, then compassion, then suffering.
edges.quote: destroys your wealth, makes you take up lying

couplets.gloss: Take up gambling and you lose your reputation, education, money, food and clothes.

edges.reason: Whoever turns to the game ends up without even food and clothing.
edges.quote: won’t come near you if you take to dice

edges.reason: Glory is on the list of what won’t come to the gambler.
edges.quote: glory

edges.reason: Learning is on the list too, among the five that stay away.
edges.quote: learning

edges.reason: Wealth is among the five that won’t come to the gambler.
edges.quote: wealth

couplets.gloss: Gamblers crave the game more with every loss, just as living beings cling tighter to life the more they suffer in it.
keywords: why losing makes you bet more

edges.reason: Shows the cruel logic of the passion: every loss makes it stronger.
edges.quote: loved more with each loss

edges.reason: Explains why losing keeps one at the table, so the urge can be seen for what it is.
edges.quote: As gambling is loved more with each loss

couplets.gloss: Each of the three bodily humours in the old medical books causes illness when it runs too high or too low.

edges.reason: Gives the sages' account of sickness: any humour pushed to an extreme brings it on.
edges.quote: would cause disease whenever they go to either extreme

couplets.gloss: You won't need medicine if you only eat once your last meal has been fully digested.

edges.reason: Makes digestion the whole of prevention: respect it and no medicine is wanted.
edges.quote: The body needs nothing called medicine

couplets.gloss: Eat sensibly and wait until your food has gone down: that's how to live a long life.

edges.reason: Measure in eating is named as the way to lengthen one's days.
edges.quote: eat knowing the measure

edges.reason: Gives someone unwell from eating a plain rule: eat in measure, and only after the last meal has gone.
edges.quote: When your food has been digested, eat knowing the measure

couplets.gloss: Wait until you're properly hungry and your last meal has gone, then eat what suits you, and not too much.

edges.reason: Real hunger and food that suits one are the conditions for a wholesome meal.
edges.quote: get properly hungry

couplets.gloss: Eat lightly and stick to foods that suit your body, and you won't have physical problems.

edges.reason: Eating sparingly of what agrees with you keeps your life free of harm.
edges.quote: stop short, and your life will come to no harm

couplets.gloss: Health comes to those who eat only on an empty stomach, just as sickness comes after those who overeat.

edges.reason: Has joy stay with the light eater and disease with the glutton.
edges.quote: disease stays with someone who gorges

couplets.gloss: Overeat beyond what your digestion can handle and your illnesses will grow out of all proportion.

edges.reason: Eating past what the body’s fire can take breeds disease without limit.
edges.quote: more than the fire can take

edges.reason: Warns the overeater that illness grows in step with the excess.
edges.quote: diseases without measure

couplets.gloss: Work out what the illness is, find its cause and the way to treat it, then go ahead carefully.
keywords: treating the cause not the symptom

edges.reason: Orders the work of cure: the illness, then its root, then the remedy.
edges.quote: Find the disease, find its cause, find the way to ease it

edges.reason: Reads as a rule for whoever treats the sick, though no healer is named.
edges.quote: act so that it works

couplets.gloss: A doctor should weigh up the patient, the illness and the time of year before beginning any treatment.

edges.reason: Tells the learned healer which three things to weigh before treating.
edges.quote: weigh the patient, the disease and the time

couplets.gloss: All treatment rests on four parties: the patient, the doctor, the drug and the pharmacist, each with four qualities of its own.

edges.reason: Lays out medicine as a fourfold whole on which every cure depends.
edges.quote: medicine has these four parts

edges.reason: Places the healer as one of the four on whom recovery rests.
edges.quote: the healer

couplets.gloss: It is said that honest dealing and a natural sense of shame are found only in those from good families.
couplets.sensitive: Says virtue comes naturally only to the well born

edges.reason: Credits good family with uprightness and shame as natural gifts.
edges.quote: do uprightness and shame come together by nature

couplets.gloss: People of good family don't slip in three things: how they behave, telling the truth and feeling shame.

edges.reason: Says those of family hold fast to this three-part standard.
edges.quote: never slip from these three

edges.reason: Correct behaviour is the first of the three they keep.
edges.quote: good conduct

edges.reason: Their word is the second thing they do not let slip.
edges.quote: truth

edges.reason: The third is the feeling that recoils from what is unworthy.
edges.quote: shame

couplets.gloss: A truly good family shows in four things: a ready smile, giving freely, pleasant words and looking down on no one.

edges.reason: Gives the four marks of those from a true family.
edges.quote: these four belong to a true family

edges.reason: Giving is the second of the four.
edges.quote: giving

edges.reason: Pleasant words come third among the marks.
edges.quote: sweet words

edges.reason: Scorning no one is the last of the four.
edges.quote: scorning no one

couplets.gloss: People of good family won't do anything that lowers them, even if offered vast sums.

edges.reason: No sum, however vast, can buy a stain on a good family's name.
edges.quote: Even for piled-up millions

couplets.gloss: People of long-standing families keep on giving generously even when they have less to give.

edges.reason: Even when what they can give has shrunk, such people stay as they were.
edges.quote: what they have to give has shrunk

edges.reason: Good nature that outlasts the means to give is offered as the mark of an old family.
edges.quote: those of an old family

couplets.gloss: Those determined to live up to their family's clean record won't stoop to trickery or shameful acts.

edges.reason: Care for a family's unstained tradition rules out deceit and low acts.
edges.quote: won’t turn to deceit and do unworthy things

couplets.gloss: A fault in someone from a respected family stands out for all to see, like the mark on the moon.

edges.reason: High birth holds a person to a standard where even one flaw is seen by all.
edges.quote: A fault in those of good family stands out

edges.reason: The spot on the moon is a small blemish that all the world can see.
edges.quote: the spot on the moon

couplets.gloss: If someone from a good family behaves unkindly, people start wondering whether he really belongs to it.
couplets.sensitive: Links rudeness with doubtful birth

edges.reason: A lack of warmth is held so far from good family that it puts a man’s birth in doubt.
edges.quote: people will doubt his family

couplets.gloss: A sprout shows you what the soil is like, and the way someone talks shows you what family they come from.

edges.reason: Makes words the test by which a man's family is known.
edges.quote: the family of a man known by the words that come out of his mouth

edges.reason: The sprout tells the soil as someone’s words tell their family.
edges.quote: A sprout shows what the soil is like

couplets.gloss: To be good you need a sense of shame, and to bring your family credit you need to treat everyone with respect.

edges.reason: Names shame as what anyone who wants goodness must have.
edges.quote: If you want goodness, have shame

edges.reason: Asks for bowing to everyone as the price of a good family name.
edges.quote: bow to everyone

ideaLinks.reason: Strife feeds the habit of drawing apart from others, which is the start of enmity.
ideaLinks.quote: feeds, in every living being, the fault of drawing apart

ideaLinks.reason: Shame turns her back on those with the fault of liquor.
ideaLinks.quote: The good woman called Shame turns her back

ideaLinks.reason: Even glory already won is lost to those in love with liquor.
Gambling destroys wealth, and nothing else brings poverty as it does.
Gambling makes you take up lying.
Gambling ruins your good name, and glory won’t come to those who take to it.
Eating in measure keeps the body free of trouble and lengthens life.
To keep a good family name you must bow to everyone.
ideaLinks.quote: If you want a good family name, bow to everyone
